findings.title: AC15 performance limits need approval
findings.problem: Spec AC15 requires before/after 30-day benchmarks and either the 825 ms target met or a documented, approved limitation. The guide records only after-figures: default sort meets it, search ~2 s, ctx_per_call ~10 s, cost 17 s, framework filter 36-38 s with intermittent 30 s timeouts. No before baseline; approval pending at MR review. Reachability not code-verifiable (spec criterion).
findings.impact: Required criterion partially met; shipping the framework filter with statement timeouts may be a regression against main.
findings.recommendation: Record before (main) figures per request type and obtain the requester's explicit decision on the documented limits.
findings.check_notes: Decision outcome and rationale mapped; main baseline recorded in guide.

fix.change: Recorded measured main vs branch baseline (7d/30d, parallel on/off) and the approved rationale in the guide and bench/README.md

decision.outcome: Approved: ship the slow sorts as documented limits, main baseline measured first
decision.rationale: Default sort (the ticket's measured case) meets 825 ms (44-150 ms vs 12-28 s on main). Search, ctx_per_call, cost and framework are bound by window-wide aggregations; a rollup or stored column (S4) is out of scope; requester approved at the Stage 6 review on 2026-11-05. Main baseline recorded in the guide's Known performance limits and bench/README.md; framework filter did not regress (main never finishes it).

findings.title: AC9 EXPLAIN evidence not recorded
findings.problem: AC9 requires EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for 7/30/90-day windows with selected-row fractions and the window token statement. run_sessions_bench.py explain mode exists but no recorded plans appear in the diff or guide.
findings.impact: Index choice and window-size behaviour are unproven for the required criterion.
findings.recommendation: Run the explain mode on the production-ratio seed and record the plans and fractions in the task folder or guide.
findings.check_notes: Three EXPLAIN artifacts non-empty; plans and fractions recorded in guide; commands exit 0.

fix.change: Ran explain mode for 7/30/90 days (fixed the bench explain spy for the shipped statements) and recorded plans, selected-row fractions and timings

findings.title: Cost-key SQL builders bloat reader.py
findings.problem: Standards (code-quality Module Cohesion, partial): reader.py is ~1866 lines and gained ~470, including the self-contained cost-key, rate-join and kind-flag SQL builders with their constants.
findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard blocks the workflow; duplicated cost-key/flag spellings are harder to keep in step.
findings.recommendation: Extract the cost-key/model-flag SQL builders and constants into their own module next to reader.py and import them.
findings.check_notes: Builders moved to cost_key_sql.py; reader.py now imports them (1719 lines).

fix.change: Moved cost-key, rate-join, kind-flag and token-group SQL builders from reader.py (-145 lines) into postgres/cost_key_sql.py

findings.title: Framework classifier twin lacks parity test
findings.problem: AC6 partial: classifier_names_by_session_sql (set-wise rewrite of CLASSIFIER_NAMES_SQL, five sources, started_at-1h bound, array_agg DISTINCT) is exercised live only via session_dims.skills; session_skills, invocations_hourly (kind 2/4, hour bound), agents and commands branches are untested against CLASSIFIER_NAMES_SQL.
findings.impact: Drift would make the framework filter list a different session set and total than each row's delivery_framework, with no failing test.
findings.recommendation: Add a live-Postgres test seeding every name source (incl. rows just before/well before started_at and a kind outside 2,4) asserting both builders return equal name arrays and get_framework_page keeps exactly the matching sessions.
findings.check_notes: New live-Postgres parity test seeds every name source and bound and checks get_framework_page.

fix.change: Added a live parity test of classifier_names_by_session_sql against CLASSIFIER_NAMES_SQL for every source and bound, and of get_framework_page's session set

findings.title: Invalid leftover index silently skipped
findings.problem: upgrade uses CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS; an invalid index of the same name left by a failed CONCURRENTLY pre-build is skipped, so migration reports success while the index is unused.
findings.impact: start_time sort stays slow after a supposedly successful deploy. Reachability: only the IF NOT EXISTS statement was read, runbook path unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Drop the index first when pg_index.indisvalid is false, then create it; apply the same to the shared-count index revision.
findings.check_notes: Migration drops an invalid index before CREATE IF NOT EXISTS; both indexes merged into a1c1a0000010.

fix.change: One revision a1c1a0000010 creates both indexes, dropping an invalid leftover of the same name first (verified live: invalid indexes rebuilt valid)
